newsitem.title: USA: Phillips Petroleum says foreign output increasing.
newsitem.headline: Phillips Petroleum says foreign output increasing.

text.p: Phillips Petroleum Co foresees increasing production from its foreign oil and natural gas investments in coming years, and will spend additional capital in the area, Wayne Allen, company chairman and CEO, said Monday.
Allen spoke to reporters at the American Petroleum Institute annual meeting, saying his company was having a "very strong year," and expects further improvement in 1997.
"Our year has been helped by oil and gas prices and basically we're expecting a strong year," Allen said.
Allen said worldwide exploration and production highlights include development of the Ekofisk block, where a well has been drilled in recent weeks at the East of Troll Field.
Allen also said the company's offshore China operations are "going extremely well," and increasing to 140,000 barrels per day from 100,000 bpd.
He said projects in Algeria, offshore United Kingdom and Nigeria also feature prominently in the company's plans.
Overall, Allen reiterated that Phillips plans to spend between $1.6 billion and $2.0 on capital expenditures for 1997.
"We could be comfortable around $2 billion, but it will be at least flat to up slightly," Allen said.
Allen also emphasized the company's interest in the Gulf of Mexico where it has recently teamed with Mobil Corp on bidding for numerous deep sea block developments.
"We've come out with 107 blocks (in deepwater Gulf of Mexico) and that's a good position to be in," Allen said, noting the company would take a measured approach to its deep water program.
